phases.message: I have a second opinion at Westbrook Spine on 30 October and need all my records before then. Start in my inbox: read what Westbrook wants and everything from the providers.
This is Alder Creek, my primary care portal. Request what Westbrook needs from here.
Clinora is Harlow Valley Hospital's records portal. Read my rights and their fees, and deal with each invoice: pay what's fair, dispute what isn't.
Patientry has Brightline's MRI images. Get mine.
Faxline. Bayside Orthopedics only takes record requests by fax. Send mine to the right number.
Back in my inbox. Answer whatever still needs an answer and leave the rest. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

rights.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Harlow Valley Hospital: your right of access to your health records under HIPAA, 45 CFR 164.524, and our copy fee schedule. Topics: access, fees, third-party.

You may get a copy of your records in the form you ask for, electronic if we hold them electronically. A provider must act on a written request within 30 calendar days of receiving it, and may extend once, by no more than 30 more days, only by telling you in writing within the first 30 days why and by what date (45 CFR 164.524(b)(2)). HHS proposed in 2021 to shorten this to 15 days; that proposal is not in effect, and 30 days applies. A provider that has neither answered nor sent an extension notice within 30 days is late.

For a copy you ask for yourself, a provider may charge only a reasonable, cost-based fee: the labor of copying, supplies, and postage when mailed. It may not charge for searching for or retrieving the records (45 CFR 164.524(c)(4)). Harlow Valley's schedule: an electronic copy of records we hold electronically, sent to you: a flat $6.50. Paper copies mailed to you: actual cost, labor at $27 an hour, paper and postage, itemized.

When you direct us to send your records to someone else, such as an insurer or a lawyer, the cost-based fee limit does not apply: a federal court vacated it for third-party directives (Ciox Health, LLC v. Azar, D.D.C. 23 January 2020), and HHS applies it only to your own request. Such copies are charged under state law and our schedule: $1.00 a page.
